SIGNS OF DEHYDRATION 
* Loss of weight 
* Sunken eyes & fontanelle 
* Dry mucous membranes 
* Thirst 
* Loss of skin turgor 
* Acidotic breathing 
* Decreased urine output 
SIGNS OF SHOCK 
* CRT > 3 secs 
* Cold peripheries 
* Thready pulses 
* Listless 
* Tachycardia 
* Decreased BP 
* Depressed LOC 
GASTROENTERITIS IN 
PAEDIATRICS 
MANAGEMENT SHOCK & SEVERE DEHYDRATION 
Resuscitation 
• ABC approach 
• Oxygen, monitors, IV line 
• Fluid bolus 20ml/kg with a crystalloid (Ringers Lactate / 0.9% Normal Saline) 
unless 
■ Severely malnourished 
■ Cardiac failure 
■ Severe pneumonia 
■ Hypernatraemia (Na+ 
■ Encephalopathy 
■ < 3 months old 
 
> 150 mmol/l) 
• Still shocked – give 10ml/kg boluses until pulse is palpable or maximum of 
60ml/kg in total has been given 
 
Correct Electrolyte Abnormalities 
• Hypokalaemia (K+ < 2.5) 15% KCl (ml) [(0.3) x (weight in kgs) x (4)] / 2 
(correct over 4 hours) 
• Hypoglycaemia 2ml/kg of 25% Dextrose (5ml 50% dextrose + 5ml NS) 
 
Indications for Antibiotics (see box) 
 
Special investigations 
• Urine dipstix & blood glucose on ALL patients 
• Blood gas (see box for indications) 
• Tailor further blood & radiological investigations to clinical findings 
 
Disposition 
• Urgent Paediatric referral 
 
INDICATIONS FOR BLOOD GAS 
* ALL severely dehydrated & shocked children 
* Malnourished 
*  Moderately dehydrated but with an atypical 
presentation 
* If IV rehydration is required 
* Complications – ileus, seizures 
 
INDICATIONS for ANTIBIOTICS 
* Severe malnutrition 
* Suspected systemic infection 
* Immunocompromised 
* Dysentery 
* Cholera with severe dehydration 
 
 
 
NB! All IV fluids must be controlled and preferably given using an 
infusion pump 
 
MANAGEMENT MILD TO MODERATE DEHYDRATION 
First Line = Oral rehydration solution (ORS) 
 
* Oral or via NGT 
* Volume according to the degree of dehydration 
* 12.5ml/kg/hr for 4 hours 
* Reassess 
- if tolerated & improving clinically ➔ Discharge 
- not tolerated & no clinical improvement ➔ Admit & 
commence IV fluids - ½ DD @ 10mls/kg/hr
